rule.name: sdlc-prerequisites
rule.description: Prerequisite validation before mode loads — at delegation time, not after the mode has started.

validation_rule.step: Before delegating to mode X: Check mode X's prerequisites per the table below.
If missing: Do NOT delegate to mode X. Delegate to the mode that produces the missing artifact instead. Include instruction to hand off to mode X when done.
If present: Delegate to mode X with all required artifacts in the message.
validation_rule.orchestrator_entry: When user provides JIRA ID or SOW (instead of a full PRD) and the chosen pipeline is greenfield, brownfield-extend, brownfield-add-feature, or brownfield-migrate: delegate to brainstorm first. Do NOT delegate directly to prd or architect. Brainstorm fetches context, presents it, deeply understands requirements with the user (Q&A/brainstorm), then hands off to prd or architect per pipeline. See .nayan/guidance/context-input-handling.md and .nayan/guidance/pipeline-entry-points.md.
validation_rule.note: Skills and mode logic load when the mode is activated. Prerequisite validation must run before that — so the mode only ever receives tasks when its inputs are ready.

direct_mode_entry.rule: When user enters this mode directly (not via workflow handoff), run expertise check on every message (per .nayan/guidance/expertise-handoff.md); if the user or Nayan asks something outside mode expertise, hand off. Then run prerequisite check before any mode work.
If prerequisites are missing: Use new_task to redirect to the mode that produces them. Do NOT proceed with mode work.
If prerequisites are present: Proceed normally.

mode.name: brainstorm
mode.prereq: User idea or draft, JIRA ID, SOW, or exploration goal — Entry mode; ask user. When user provides JIRA or SOW (instead of PRD), orchestrator delegates to brainstorm first for greenfield and brownfield (extend, add-feature, migrate). See .nayan/guidance/context-input-handling.md.

mode.name: prd
mode.prereq: User idea or draft (initial phase) — Entry mode; ask user

User idea must be structured (problem statement, users, key capabilities) OR from brainstorm handoff. If minimal (one-line, vague): delegate to brainstorm first — do NOT delegate to prd. When user provides JIRA or SOW (instead of full PRD): orchestrator delegates to brainstorm first; do NOT delegate to prd until brainstorm has handed off. See .nayan/guidance/expertise-handoff.md and context-input-handling.md.
initial-prd.md (refinement phase) — From PRD initial phase

mode.name: architect
mode.prereq: refined-prd.md with Sign-Off all three roles Approved, Approver Name, and Sign-Off Date filled — Redirect to prd; reject if Pending, Needs Revision, or missing Name/Date

condensed scope or migration brief (brownfield extend/migrate) — From orchestrator, or from brainstorm handoff when user provided JIRA/SOW (brainstorm includes aligned scope in message). If missing: ask user or redirect to orchestrator/brainstorm
existing architecture.md or legacy system context (for brownfield-migrate) — Ask user for path; cannot extend/migrate without it
codebase access — Ask user for repo path
mode.note: Architecture phase only. For brownfield-migrate: migration brief or condensed scope; legacy architecture or system context acceptable. See plan_input_requirements rule for full input requirements.

mode.name: plan
mode.prereq: architecture.md — Redirect to architect
refined-prd.md (greenfield) or condensed scope (brownfield) — Redirect to prd or architect
UX artifacts (when UI, dev-plan phase): one prototype per persona — Redirect to prototype
mode.note: Dev-plan phase only. Plan produces development-plan.md from architecture.md and PRD/scope.

mode.name: prototype
mode.prereq: architecture.md — Redirect to architect
refined-prd.md (greenfield) or condensed scope (brownfield) — Redirect to prd or ask user
CONTEXT (greenfield|brownfield) — Infer from inputs or ask user
mode.note: Only when the solution involves UI. Architect delegates to prototype when UI is involved; otherwise to plan (dev-plan phase).

mode.name: code
mode.prereq: development-plan.md — Redirect to plan
architecture.md — Redirect to architect

mode.name: qa
mode.prereq: development-plan.md (or bug-fix-scope for brownfield-fix-bug or refactor-scope for brownfield-refactor) — Redirect to plan or code
Codebase — Redirect to code
mode.note: QA runs phases: code review (first pass), QA plan creation, QA execution, code quality gate, code review (second pass). For brownfield-fix-bug simple fixes: QA may skip plan/execution phases. tester and sdet are methodologies within qa-planning skill. When using sdet: test-cases.md or manual specs required; ask user for Java/Python.

mode.name: secure
mode.prereq: development-plan.md (or bug-fix-scope for brownfield-fix-bug) — Redirect to plan or code
Codebase — Redirect to code
Code quality gate passed — Redirect to qa — do not skip
mode.note: Brownfield: VERACODE_API_ID, VERACODE_API_KEY, Java 11+ required. See code_quality_security_gates rule. This mode cannot be skipped. Brownfield-fix-bug: no development-plan; bug-fix-scope (or fix context from code/QA) satisfies context prerequisite.

mode.name: deploy
mode.prereq: architecture.md — Redirect to architect; optional for brownfield-fix-bug (proceed with codebase + security-review)
Codebase — Redirect to code
security-review.md — Redirect to secure — do not skip
code-review.md — Redirect to qa — do not skip
All sprints finished (or fix complete for brownfield-fix-bug) — Do not proceed; inform user to complete code first
Deployment target — Ask user before proceeding
mode.note: Secure and qa (quality gate) are mandatory; do not proceed without both passing. Brownfield-fix-bug: no development-plan/sprints; fix completion from code is sufficient.

mode.name: debug (Brownfield C – fix-bug, debug phase)
mode.prereq: Bug report / description — Ask user
Codebase access — Ask user for repo path

mode.name: code (Brownfield C – fix-bug entry)
mode.prereq: Bug report / description — Ask user; when handed off from debug: diagnosis and fix instructions in message satisfy this
Codebase access — Ask user for repo path

mode.name: qa (Brownfield D – refactor entry)
mode.prereq: Refactor request from user (QA produces refactor-scope when entry) — Ask user
Codebase access — Ask user for repo path

row.validates: brainstorm, prd, architect, plan, prototype, debug, code, qa
row.check: Entry-mode prerequisites; when JIRA/SOW (not full PRD) and pipeline greenfield or brownfield extend/add-feature/migrate: delegate to brainstorm first
Structured concept or aligned scope in message; pipelineId and CONTEXT included when handing off
architecture.md, PRD/scope in message (prototype when UI; plan dev-plan when API-only)
diagnosis + fix instructions in message (debug phase hands off to code implementation phase)
architecture.md, PRD/scope, UX artifacts in message
development-plan.md (or BUG_FIX_SCOPE when pipeline brownfield-fix-bug), codebase in message
development-plan.md (or BUG_FIX_SCOPE when pipeline brownfield-fix-bug), codebase, code-review.md in message
architecture.md, codebase, security-review.md, code-review.md in message

rule.redirect_template: Prerequisites for [current-mode] are missing. Redirecting to [producing-mode] first. Missing: [list artifacts] [Producing-mode], please produce [artifact(s)]. When complete and user has approved, hand off to [current-mode] with context: [brief context]. Original request: [user's original request]
